title: the daily routine (dinacharya)
hook: the chapter that cleans your teeth also tells you to greet people first

segments.voice: Yesterday, the daily routine, dinacharya, put effort in measure: vyayama, to half one's strength, stopped while something's left. Where did you stop one step early? Day one thousand two hundred ninety-eight.

Same chapter, a few verses on. The Ashtanga Hridaya has just finished with teeth, eyes, oil, exercise and the bath. A reader might expect the next topic to be breakfast. Instead, the text turns to people. How to speak. Whom to help. What happiness is for. A health manual, still inside its chapter on the daily routine, starts talking about kindness, as if it were part of the same morning. In the tradition's eyes, it is. Today: good conduct as part of the day.
screen: `TEETH, EYES, OIL, EXERCISE, BATH.` → `THEN THE TEXT TURNS TO PEOPLE.` → `KINDNESS IN THE SAME CHAPTER.`

segments.voice: Ayurveda has a name for this: sadvritta, good conduct. In the Ashtanga Hridaya it sits right inside the daily routine. Here it is, paraphrased. Every action of every being is aimed at happiness. But happiness doesn't come without dharma, without right living. So be devoted to dharma. That's a striking move for a medical text. It doesn't separate the healthy body from the good life. It says the one depends on the other. Then the text gets practical about speech, which is where a lot of conduct happens. Paraphrased again: speak at the right time. Say what's helpful, and say it in measure. Don't contradict yourself. Make it pleasant to hear. And be the one who speaks first, with a friendly face. That last pair is easy to skip past, and it may be the easiest thing in the chapter to try. Greet first. Don't wait for the other person to decide whether this is going to be warm. Look at where that puts kindness: in the same list as brushing your teeth. Not a grand virtue for special occasions. Daily upkeep. It also echoes Sushruta's healthy person, whose self, senses and mind are clear and content. A day of sharp words and cold silences doesn't leave a mind like that. And it's specific. Not be nice. Right time, helpful, measured, pleasant, first. Those are things a person can actually try before lunch. Ayurveda's daily round, it turns out, doesn't end at the skin.
screen: `SADVRITTA: GOOD CONDUCT` · `NO HAPPINESS WITHOUT DHARMA` · `RIGHT TIME, HELPFUL, MEASURED` · `GREET FIRST, WITH A FRIENDLY FACE`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: rehearse one greeting. Let the body be still for a moment. Bring to mind someone you'll likely see today or tomorrow: at home, at work, in a shop. Someone you usually wait for, or barely greet. See yourself speaking first. See the face you'd want to bring. Let it be warm, not forced. Notice what happens in the body when you picture it. Then let the picture go, and rest in the breath. If you pray, you can hold that person in your prayer for a moment. The bell holds the time.
The daily routine. In the Ashtanga Hridaya it includes sadvritta, good conduct: speak helpfully, in measure, at the right time, and be the first to greet. Today's word.
Your line: the daily routine, dinacharya. Today, with one person you'd usually wait for, be the one who speaks first, with a friendly face. Day one thousand two hundred ninety-eight.

howItsDone: Ayurvedic texts include sadvritta, good conduct, in the daily routine, and practitioners treat truthful, kind and timely speech as part of a healthy day alongside diet and exercise.

match.prompt: good conduct in the round — tap the pairs.

myth: the daily routine in Ayurveda is only about the body
the Ashtanga Hridaya's daily routine chapter turns to conduct: speech, help, and dharma.
the text says happiness doesn't come without dharma
every being seeks happiness, it says, and that needs right living.
the text's advice on speech is just 'be nice'
it's specific: the right time, helpful, measured, not self-contradicting, pleasant, and greet first.

fork.setup: a coworker walks in. you're both tired, and neither of you has said a word yet. what does the Ashtanga Hridaya's good conduct suggest?
options: wait and see what mood they're in.
be the first to speak, with a friendly face.
say nothing until you have something clever.
fork.reveal: the text's advice on speech ends right there: speak at the right time, helpfully, in measure, and be the first to speak, with a pleasant face.

original.note: Sanskrit sadvritta: good conduct, the ethical part of Ayurveda's daily routine.

trapdoor: what you thought: a health routine stops at the skin.
what it means: the classical daily round includes how you speak and treat people.
what a scholar hears: sadvritta in the Ashtanga Hridaya: all action seeks happiness, happiness needs dharma, so speak timely, helpful, measured, and greet first.
